question: What is the main use of labetalol in pregnancy?

options.A: Lowering blood pressure safely during pregnancy
options.B: Stopping premature contractions in preterm labour
options.C: Preventing postpartum infection after a C-section
options.D: Inducing cervical ripening before formal induction

explanation: Labetalol is commonly used in midwifery to manage high blood pressure disorders like pre-eclampsia without harming the baby. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T2#BMP213_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why do midwives prefer labetalol over older blood pressure drugs during pregnancy?

options.A: It lowers blood pressure smoothly while maintaining placental blood flow
options.B: It has zero side effects for either the mother or the developing baby
options.C: It completely cures gestational hypertension within twenty-four hours
options.D: It can be administered exclusively by traditional birth attendants

explanation: Labetalol controls maternal blood pressure gently without cutting off the vital blood supply to the placenta. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T2#BMP213_U3_T2_h1)

question: Which two receptor types does labetalol block to lower blood pressure?
explanation: Labetalol blocks alpha-1 receptors on blood vessels and beta receptors on the heart to reduce blood pressure effectively. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T2#BMP213_U3_T2_h2)

question: What happens when labetalol blocks alpha-1 receptors on blood vessels?

options.A: The vessels constrict and blood pressure shoots up
options.B: Heart rate increases rapidly to compensate for volume
options.C: Blood flow to all internal organs completely stops
options.D: The vessels dilate and peripheral resistance decreases

explanation: Blocking alpha-1 receptors relaxes and widens blood vessels so blood flows through more easily. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T2#BMP213_U3_T2_h2)

question: At what blood pressure reading is labetalol urgently given to prevent a stroke in pregnancy?
explanation: Readings of 160/110 mmHg or higher are considered severe hypertension in pregnancy and require urgent treatment. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T2#BMP213_U3_T2_h3)

question: A pregnant woman at 34 weeks arrives at the ward with a blood pressure of 170/115 mmHg. What is the best immediate action?

options.A: A routine daily iron and folate supplement
options.D: An oxytocic agent for uterine contraction

explanation: Severely high blood pressure requires immediate blood pressure-lowering drugs like labetalol to protect the mother. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T2#BMP213_U3_T2_h3)

question: Which class of blood pressure medications is avoided in pregnancy because it causes birth defects?
explanation: ACE inhibitors are avoided in pregnancy due to risks to the baby, making labetalol a much safer alternative. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T2#BMP213_U3_T2_h4)

question: What mild side effect might a newborn experience if the mother took labetalol right up until delivery?

options.A: Multiple limb deformities and missing fingers
options.B: Transient low blood sugar or low heart rate
options.C: Permanent hearing loss and profound deafness
options.D: Complete failure of the lungs to develop

explanation: Because labetalol crosses the placenta, some babies show temporary signs like a slightly low heart rate or blood sugar after birth. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T2#BMP213_U3_T2_h4)

question: What is a standard starting dose of oral labetalol for managing high blood pressure in pregnancy?
explanation: Oral labetalol therapy usually starts at 100 mg twice daily and is adjusted upward as needed. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T2#BMP213_U3_T2_h5)

question: Why is close monitoring needed when giving intravenous labetalol for severe pre-eclampsia?

options.A: To ensure the intravenous cannula never leaks fluid onto skin
options.B: To measure the exact volume of urine produced every minute
options.C: To prevent blood pressure from dropping too fast or too low
options.D: To check if the patient is developing gestational diabetes mellitus

explanation: Intravenous medication acts quickly, so tight monitoring is vital to avoid dropping the mother's blood pressure too drastically. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T2#BMP213_U3_T2_h5)

question: What unusual physical sensation do some pregnant women report when taking labetalol?
explanation: Scalp tingling is a known, harmless side effect that some patients experience when starting labetalol. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T2#BMP213_U3_T2_h6)

question: A midwife is about to give oral labetalol and finds the patient's pulse is 54 beats per minute. What should the midwife do?

options.A: Withhold the medication and notify the doctor
options.B: Encourage the patient to drink hot coffee quickly
options.C: Administer the medication as prescribed anyway
options.D: Double the dose to stimulate the heart muscle

explanation: A heart rate below 60 beats per minute means the dose should be held until a clinician reviews the patient. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T2#BMP213_U3_T2_h6)

question: Which medical condition is a strict reason not to use labetalol?
explanation: Beta-blockers like labetalol can cause severe tightening of the airways, making them unsafe for women with asthma. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T2#BMP213_U3_T2_h7)

question: Why must a midwife carefully check a patient's medical history before giving labetalol?

options.A: To avoid triggering respiratory failure in women with hidden or known asthma
options.B: To guarantee the baby will be born with a higher than average birth weight
options.C: To prevent the development of permanent postpartum kidney damage
options.D: To make sure the patient has enough money to buy extra malaria drugs

explanation: Screening for asthma is critical because labetalol can trigger a dangerous asthma attack in susceptible individuals. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T2#BMP213_U3_T2_h7)
